flags.detail: The key (D) is correct and was verified: extracting an int or a std::string from an exhausted stream sets eofbit AND failbit (bad=0), and the stream then tests false. But the explanation states that failbit 'is the bit a stream's boolean conversion actually reports'. That is a false generalisation. std::basic_ios::operator bool returns !fail(), and fail() is (rdstate() & (failbit | badbit)) != 0. Verified by experiment: a stream with ONLY badbit set (in3.setstate(std::ios::badbit)) also reports fail()==1 and converts to false. As written, the sentence teaches that badbit does not affect the boolean test, which is wrong, and it sits awkwardly beside distractor A which is specifically about badbit. Fix: change '...failbit, which is the bit a stream's boolean conversion actually reports' to '...failbit; the stream's boolean conversion reports !fail(), i.e. it is false when failbit OR badbit is set, and eofbit alone never makes it false'. That still cleanly discriminates D from B while being accurate.
flags.suggested: Keep key D. Reword the explanation's second clause to: the boolean conversion is !fail(), which is false when failbit or badbit is set — eofbit on its own does not make a stream test false.

notes: One low-severity explanation flag out of 12; no wrong keys found. I did not take the keys on trust — the six questions that turn on an exact C++ behaviour were compiled and run under g++ 13.3 (-std=c++17): member destruction order prints CBA (ebec27 key D); delete through a non-virtual base pointer runs only ~Base while a virtual base dtor runs ~Derived then ~Base, and marking only the derived dtor virtual still runs only ~Base (91c240 key A); a reference member assigned in the constructor body is a hard compile error while pointer and int members assign fine (f591a5 key B); ifstream has no seekp and tellg takes no argument (both distractors are ill-formed) while seekg(-20, ios::cur) moved the get pointer 30 -> 10 (0b2d3a key C); ofstream opened with ios::ate ALONE truncated 'HELLO' to 'X', ios::app + seekp(0) still appended giving 'HELLOX', and fstream in|out|ate preserved and overwrote in place giving 'HXLLO' — so e01c9b's key A and its unusually specific explanation are both right; catch-by-value sliced Deriv to Base while catch-by-reference kept Deriv, and a bare rethrow from a by-value handler still delivered Deriv to the outer handler, so distractor C is genuinely false (9360f4 key B); base-before-derived handler ordering compiles (warning only, -Wexceptions) and the BASE handler ran, which also confirms distractor D's 'ill-formed' claim is wrong (9cdfbf key C); at(9) on a 5-char string threw std::out_of_range while s[9] tripped the _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS bounds assert, confirming UB (83968b key D). One judgement call I considered and decided against flagging: in b5ce17, distractor C 'private virtual inheritance' brushes against the real is-implemented-in-terms-of idiom, but the gratuitous 'virtual' plus the stem's normative 'should the design use' leave composition unambiguously best. This batch is markedly cleaner than the earlier 51 — the correct-key-via-false-rule failure mode showed up once, and only as an over-broad clause rather than an invented rule.
